title: Adoption of out-of-order execution
decision: Implement aggressive out-of-order execution with a large instruction window, breaking from the strictly in-order design of the 21164
alternatives_or_rejected: Continuing with in-order execution and relying on the compiler to statically schedule instructions and hide latencies
rationale: Compiler scheduling alone could not adequately hide memory and branch latencies in the face of cache misses and unpredictable run-time behavior; dynamic out-of-order execution was necessary to extract more instruction-level parallelism
outcome: Higher performance on irregular and memory-intensive code, at the cost of significantly increased design complexity, die area, and power

title: Tournament (hybrid) branch predictor
decision: Use a tournament predictor that dynamically selects between a local-history predictor and a global-history predictor on a per-branch basis
alternatives_or_rejected: A simple bimodal predictor, or relying exclusively on either pure local-history or pure global-history prediction alone
rationale: No single prediction mechanism is best for all programs; some branches are best predicted by local patterns while others benefit from global correlation, so an adaptive chooser yields higher overall accuracy
outcome: Improved prediction accuracy that helped mitigate the penalty of the deep pipeline on mispredicted branches

title: Deep pipeline optimized for clock frequency
decision: Employ a deep seven-stage integer pipeline (and deeper floating-point pipes) targeting very high clock frequency rather than maximizing IPC in a shallow pipeline
alternatives_or_rejected: A shorter pipeline with fewer stages that would achieve better CPI at a more modest clock rate
rationale: Process technology trends and competitive pressure favored raw clock speed; simpler, shorter-latency pipe stages allowed initial operation at 600 MHz with headroom toward 1 GHz and beyond
outcome: Industry-leading clock frequency at introduction, though with a larger branch-misprediction penalty due to the greater number of stages to flush

title: Large physical register files for renaming
where_in_paper: Integer and floating-point execution / Register files
decision: Provide 80 physical integer registers and 72 physical floating-point registers to support register renaming and speculative execution
alternatives_or_rejected: Smaller physical register files that would limit the number of in-flight instructions, or avoiding register renaming altogether
rationale: Four-wide integer issue, two-wide floating-point issue, and aggressive out-of-order speculation require many physical registers to hold temporary results and checkpointed architectural state across branches
outcome: Enough register capacity and bandwidth to sustain high instruction throughput and deep speculation windows

title: Off-chip L2 cache with on-chip controller
decision: Move the L2 cache data arrays off-chip (using external SRAMs controlled by an on-chip tag and controller) rather than integrating L2 SRAMs on the processor die as in the 21164
alternatives_or_rejected: Retaining an on-chip L2 cache in the same manner as the Alpha 21164
rationale: The die area consumed by out-of-order logic, large register files, and wide issue left insufficient room for on-chip L2 SRAMs; external SRAMs also permitted larger, flexible L2 sizes and leveraged commodity memory technology
outcome: Support for large L2 configurations (up to 16 MB) but with higher access latency than an on-die L2
